subject.title: [Feature]: cron jobs.d/ directory support (one file per job, for NixOS/GitOps declarative setups)

question: Should OpenClaw core add a `jobs.d`/`storeDir` declarative cron file surface, or should this remain an external sync/plugin/API workflow on top of SQLite?
rationale: The request adds a new cron storage/config workflow that intersects with the current SQLite runtime contract, config compatibility policy, path-safety concerns, and the newer declaration-key API; automation should not choose that product boundary alone.

options.title: Keep as product design item
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers decide the core-vs-plugin direction and the required compatibility/security contract.

options.title: Route to external sync/plugin
options.body: Use `declarationKey` plus CLI/Gateway APIs as the supported import target and keep file watching or NixOS activation sync outside core.

options.title: Sponsor a core import/sync surface
options.body: Approve a core design that documents load/sync/delete precedence, preserves SQLite runtime state, handles path trust, and covers doctor, docs, and focused cron tests.

recommendation.title: Keep as product design item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers decide the core-vs-plugin direction and the required compatibility/security contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent cron SQLite migration and declaration-key work make steipete the clearest routing candidate for the storage/product-boundary choice.
